subject: Vocational
title: The Mission
subtitle: Products and services display
objective_verbatim: Produce a poster or display showing the range of products and services provided by different hospitality businesses.

source.alias_note: Neutral source alias; original workbook unchanged and not included.

mapping.verification: Activity alignment checked against the official student-book sample printed page 8: magazine/brochure-based products-and-services display across different businesses. The numeric four-products/four-services/two-business checks and A3 format are local workbook teaching criteria. [VERIFY] equivalence to the owner’s cited edition and assessor acceptance of illustrated material in place of printed-media resources. Achievement is not automatic.

evidence.description: Individual A3 poster or display, with its photo reference and classroom-check record.
evidence.ownership: The learner selects, arranges and labels the items. Adults may read, pre-cut, place to the learner’s directions or scribe exact words, recording support.
checklist: At least four products and four services.
Every item has a business and product/service label.
Learner circles ideas their own café could offer.
Photo reference, date and ownership recorded.
Any justified mixed-offer classification is explained.

evidence_ownership: Learner supplies choices, labels and reasons. Adults may read, rephrase, pre-cut or scribe exact words; support is recorded. A model, blank template or class activity is not automatically completed individual evidence.

vocab.meaning: An item or offer that a customer can buy.
vocab.cue: A labelled item or room offer.

vocab.meaning: An action done for a customer.
A list of food and drink on offer.
A small booklet that gives information.
The variety of things on offer.
Information arranged for other people to see.

stages.title: The Mission
body: Products and services display
How can a labelled display show what hospitality businesses offer?
Use your own display plan.
stages.notes: Untimed. Bring forward the learner’s Week 2 Theory plan and checked sort. This task makes an individual A3 poster or display panel, not a whole-class product. Source: sources/MTP.xlsx; revision sha256:0895674f2901b602daf998b8a7aa1516522ce0c301b23bfba941fcc1807977cd. Medium Term Plan!D7; Lesson register!F9.

stages.title: Arrival task
body: A hotel breakfast: product, service or both?
What does range mean?
Scissors are on the table edge. What do you do?
What is missing from a poster with no labels?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a reset if needed.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer water, quiet breathing, a brief pause or a quieter seat without requiring a public colour disclosure. Privately agree one return action. Expected: the food is a product in the lesson convention; preparing or serving it is an associated service, so explain if saying both; range means variety; stop and ask the adult to make the scissors safe, follow local handling instructions; labels explain what the pictures mean and the business/category. Do not demonstrate unsafe handling. Individual stations; no pair work or cold calling. Adults may read, rephrase or scribe exact learner words and record support. They do not choose the learner’s assessed sort, labels or explanation. Only VF, WS, I, NS, E and R are used; confirm local code definitions before marking. Blank templates and copied models are not completed individual evidence.

stages.title: Which poster helps the reader?
body: Compare a labelled model with an unlabelled model.
Which one tells you the business and the category?
A useful label says what the item is.
This label helps because __.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Show both read-only model layouts. The weak one has pictures/items but no business or category labels; the strong one gives the reader those labels. These are teaching examples, not completed learner work. A clear label matters more than decoration.

stages.title: Today I can
body: Produce a poster or display showing the range of products and services provided by different hospitality businesses.
I can choose a range.
I can label each item clearly.
I can explain a product and a service.
stages.notes: Untimed. Read the exact supplied outcome. [QUAL] — planner mapping. Four products, four services, two business types and every item labelled are the workbook’s classroom success checks. They are not presented as unverified official criterion wording.

stages.title: Cut place and label
body: Choose three items from a supplied brochure or menu.
Place them under a business heading.
Label the item and product or service.
Model: Café — sandwich — product.
Model: Hotel — room cleaning — service.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Model safe cutting or use pre-cut materials, then place and label three items: café sandwich product, hotel room cleaning service, event catering food delivery service. Use supplied magazines, brochures, menus or leaflets; if only the illustrated bank is available, record the flat-illustration adaptation rather than claiming real brochures were used. The workbook teaches room as a product but suggests “can you hold it?” as the test. This lesson keeps the room as a bookable hotel offer sold to a guest, with booking and cleaning as services. Holding is a clue for many physical products, not a defining rule. A room/stay combines an offer and services. Accept a well-reasoned alternative classification and record the reason; do not mark a learner wrong merely for noticing the mixed offer.

stages.title: Our display checks
body: At least four products.
At least four services.
At least two business types.
Every item labelled.
Point to one product and one service.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Agree the four source classroom checks and apply them to the strong and weak model layouts. Hinge: a display has eight pictures but only one business type and no service labels. Does it meet the checks? Expected no; add another business type, show service examples and label the items. Different mixed-offer choices are acceptable with a reason.

visual.caption: At least two business types. Every item labelled.

stages.title: Your A3 display
body: Use magazines, brochures, menus, leaflets or the supplied cut outs.
Choose and arrange your own items.
Supported: use pre-cut pictures and labels.
Independent: create your own clear layout.
Aspire: add the job role that provides each item or service.
stages.notes: 12 minutes. First part of the 18-minute individual task. Learners work at individual stations, using their checked plan. At 10 minutes into the individual work, check the four criteria and record independence. Adult help is practical access support, not permission to select or label the learner’s assessed items. Keep scissors and glue under the school’s ordinary supervision procedures.

route_tasks.Supported: Choose pre-cut images and use the label bank. MCQ: place labelled cards under business headings.
route_tasks.Independent: Select, arrange and label your own range of items.
route_tasks.Aspire: Match each product or service to the job role that provides it.

stages.title: Check and capture your evidence
body: Count products, services and business types.
Check every label.
Circle ideas our own café could offer.
Supported: point through the checks with an adult.
Independent: explain one change you made.
Aspire: justify one café idea.
stages.notes: 6 minutes. Completes the 18-minute You Do. VOC2-L2-E1 includes the learner’s A3 poster/display and real photo reference. Ask the learner to identify one product and one service and explain any ambiguous offer. An adult captures the actual work with approved equipment; learners need no phones. Record support and actual contribution. The café idea is a proposed choice, not an already approved menu or promise to prepare food.

route_tasks.Supported: Point to each category and check labels with an adult reader.
route_tasks.Independent: Check the four criteria and improve one unclear label.
route_tasks.Aspire: Explain why a selected idea could suit the café and what needs checking.

stages.title: Tidy and file
body: Put tools away safely.
Keep your display and photo reference together.
Record one café idea you circled.
I improved __.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. Tidy, photograph and file using the approved workflow in the evidence app. The photo must show the learner’s own display and readable labels; capture date and reference only after it exists. Check actual ownership, access support and active minutes. Do not automatically tick an award challenge complete or assume planned time was earned.

stages.title: Exit ticket
body: Show one labelled product and one labelled service.
Name the business for each.
The __ is a product. __ is a service.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Private adult check, pointing or a short written response. Accept accurate examples and any defensible mixed-offer explanation. If the label or business is unclear, the next step is to improve that exact label. No whole-class performance is required.

stages.title: Key words
body: Product: an item or offer a customer can buy.
Service: an action done for a customer.
Menu: food and drink on offer.
Brochure: a small information booklet.
Range: variety.
Display: information arranged for others to see.
stages.notes: Untimed vocabulary reference. Read the labels and the frame “The __ business offers __.” Words, item labels and pictures carry the category; colour alone never decides product or service.

support_pages.title: Display label bank
lines: Cut apart, copy or point. Add the chosen item name to each label.
Café — __________ — product
Café — __________ — service
Hotel — __________ — product
Hotel — __________ — service
Event catering — __________ — product
Event catering — __________ — service
My item is __. Its business is __. I chose product/service because __.

support_pages.title: Strong labelled model layout
lines: Read-only teaching model. Your display uses your own selections and arrangement.
CAFÉ PRODUCTS: sandwich; coffee. CAFÉ SERVICES: taking an order; clearing a table.
HOTEL PRODUCTS: room offer; breakfast. HOTEL SERVICES: booking a room; cleaning a room.
The model has four products, four services, two business types and each item labelled. It follows the workbook convention for the room offer.
Use pictures/cut outs with the labels. If you explain a mixed offer differently, give a reason.

support_pages.title: Weak unlabelled model layout
lines: Read-only comparison example.
Sandwich · coffee · room picture · breakfast · booking · cleaning · order · table.
No business headings or product/service labels are given. The reader cannot clearly follow the categories.
Which labels and groupings would help? Do not file this model as your own poster.

support_pages.title: Display route prompts
lines: Supported: choose pre-cut pictures and use the label bank. MCQ access: place pre-labelled items under business headings.
Independent: choose and arrange your own range from the supplied materials.
Aspire: add the job role that provides each product or service.
Check: four products, four services, two business types and every item labelled.
Circle an idea our own café could offer. This is a proposal; ingredients, costs, equipment and approval still need checking before any later practical work.
Frame: I chose __ for our café because __. One thing to check is __.

evidence_pages.title: My display evidence record
instructions: Keep this record with your own A3 poster or display and its photo reference.
Identify one product and one service, name the business and circle ideas for our café on your display.
fields: My room or mixed-offer reason if needed: ____________________

instructions: Check your own display. Improve an unclear label or category before the photo is captured.
fields: [ ] I show at least four products.

planner_sections.heading: Purpose and source
paragraphs: Exact outcome: Produce a poster or display showing the range of products and services provided by different hospitality businesses. Source: Medium Term Plan!D7 and Lesson register!F9. This is Autumn 2 Week 2 Mission. Actual teaching date remains blank.

The learner makes their own A3 poster or display panel, then circles possible ideas for the later café. The source classroom checks are at least four products, four services, two business types and every item labelled.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split practice 12 and evidence 6; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Reference slides are untimed. Check the criteria at ten minutes into the individual task and record independence.

planner_sections.heading: Before the lesson
paragraphs: Bring each learner’s checked sort and display plan. Prepare A3 paper or display panels, safe scissors, glue, supplied magazines/brochures/menus/leaflets and pre-cut access materials. Labelled cut outs are available as support. An adult uses approved camera equipment for evidence.

If flat illustrations replace the workbook’s printed-media format, state this as an access/source adaptation; do not claim a real brochure or menu was used when it was not. No food is prepared in this lesson.

planner_sections.heading: Classification and modelling
paragraphs: The workbook teaches room as a product but suggests “can you hold it?” as the test. This lesson keeps the room as a bookable hotel offer sold to a guest, with booking and cleaning as services. Holding is a clue for many physical products, not a defining rule. A room/stay combines an offer and services. Accept a well-reasoned alternative classification and record the reason; do not mark a learner wrong merely for noticing the mixed offer.

Show a labelled and an unlabelled model. Model cutting or selecting, placing and labelling three items. Emphasise business type, item name and product/service wording. Decorative quality is secondary to a readable range and accurate explanation.

planner_sections.heading: Evidence and ownership
paragraphs: VOC2-L2-E1 includes the individual A3 poster/display, its classroom checklist and actual photo reference. The learner chooses the items, categories and café ideas. Adults may pre-cut, read or scribe exact words and place materials to the learner’s direction, with support recorded.

The workbook calls this the second part of its mapped activity. Do not treat a blank template, copied teaching model or planned duration as completed individual evidence. Exact official criterion wording and edition equivalence remain [VERIFY] unless separately confirmed.

planner_sections.heading: Teaching and access
paragraphs: Arrival: the breakfast food is a product and serving it is a service; range means variety; make scissors safe through adult help; labels tell the reader what an item represents. Hinge: eight unlabelled pictures from one business do not meet the workbook classroom checks.

Supported uses pre-cut images and a label bank; MCQ access places labelled items under business headings. Independent designs the layout. Aspire matches products/services to job roles and explains a café idea. Check at ten minutes, name the actual gap and ask the learner to improve it.

planner_sections.heading: Regulation and learner voice
paragraphs: BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer water, quiet breathing, a brief pause or a quieter seat without requiring a public colour disclosure. Privately agree one return action.

Individual stations; no pair work or cold calling. Adults may read, rephrase or scribe exact learner words and record support. They do not choose the learner’s assessed sort, labels or explanation. Only VF, WS, I, NS, E and R are used; confirm local code definitions before marking. Blank templates and copied models are not completed individual evidence.

Lundy Space: individual workstation. Voice: the learner selects range and café ideas. Audience: the adult reads the labels and listens to an explanation. Influence: the learner makes one specific improvement after feedback.

planner_sections.heading: Café link and recording
paragraphs: Circled café items are proposals, not an approved menu. Later checks will cover suitability, ingredients, costs, equipment and permissions. Do not infer a practical-food commitment or a pupil’s answer.

Planned hospitality time is 40 minutes. Actual date, active minutes, evidence reference, support and initials remain blank until taught. Follow the workbook’s agreed-Plan rule and keep Careers minutes separate. File actual work in the evidence app.

staff_answers: The classroom display checks are at least four products, four services, two business types and every item labelled. These are source workbook checks, not a quotation of unverified official criteria.

Strong model: café sandwich/coffee as products and taking an order/clearing a table as services; hotel room offer/breakfast as products and booking/cleaning as services. It supplies four of each across two businesses.
Weak model lacks business headings and category labels. A learner can improve it by grouping and naming items, then explaining the product or action.

A hotel breakfast may combine the food product with preparation or serving services. A room/stay is also a mixed offer; accept a well-reasoned alternative explanation instead of imposing the holding clue as a universal rule.

A café proposal might be a sandwich or customer welcome. The learner supplies the idea and reason. Further suitability, cost, ingredient and equipment checks belong to later planning; no menu or approval is assumed.
Capture readable individual work with an actual photo reference, date and support record. Record the ten-minute criteria check and independence without inventing completion or minutes.

Circle ideas our own café could offer.
display_template.footer: Circle café ideas and explain one choice in your evidence record. I · S · C

Individual stations; no pair work or cold calling. Adults may read, rephrase or scribe exact learner words and record support. They do not choose the learner’s assessed sort, labels or explanation. Only VF, WS, I, NS, E and R are used; confirm local code definitions before marking. Blank templates and copied models are not completed individual evidence.

Lundy Space: individual workstation. Voice: the learner selects range and café ideas. Audience: the adult reads the labels and listens to an explanation. Influence: the learner makes one specific improvement after feedback.

planner_sections.heading: Café link and recording
paragraphs: Circled café items are proposals, not an approved menu. Later checks will cover suitability, ingredients, costs, equipment and permissions. Do not infer a practical-food commitment or a pupil’s answer.

Planned hospitality time is 40 minutes. Actual date, active minutes, evidence reference, support and initials remain blank until taught. Follow the workbook’s agreed-Plan rule and keep Careers minutes separate. File actual work in the evidence app.

minutes_record.policy: Record actual eligible work after the agreed Plan. Do not infer time or completed evidence from a blank template.
